author: runtime_review
problem: spool called the original project_row for every row of both inputs. project_row allocated a new Map and cloned each column name per row before serialization. This candidate retains only that per-layout container and column keys between rows; it does not reduce compared data.

design.single_owner: RowProjection::project is the sole SQL ValueRef -> serde_json Value match. Legacy project_row constructs a fresh projector, calls that same owner and moves the Object out. Streaming uses one projector for one spool.
design.column_layout: cols is an immutable borrowed slice produced by the unchanged columns(source,table) and used by the unchanged SELECT. Each spool/table/side constructs its own projector. No schema cache or cross-table/state reuse is introduced.
design.lazy_keys: new creates an empty Map. Keys first allocate inside project, which in production streaming is called only after unchanged row-count and check_row_size admission. Empty tables do not preallocate all keys or row bodies.
design.reuse: get_mut replaces each existing slot; only a not-yet-seen key is cloned/inserted. Exact column iteration/insertion order is preserved for both ordinary sorted Map and preserve_order feature behavior.
design.value_semantics: The original Null, Integer(json!), Real(json!), Text(strict UTF8 then json!), Blob({blob_digest:manifest::digest}) branches are retained in the single owner. No field projection, number normalization, hash shortcut or custom JSON encoder.
design.serialization: serde_json::to_string(&Map<String,Value>) uses the same Map serialization used by Value::Object(Map). Independent literal expected tests pin result values/bytes; original strings sorted/compared exactly as before.
design.value_lifetime: serialize_row obtains the same owned serialized String, resets every Map value to Null, then returns that String. Column keys/map nodes remain, old text/blob-derived Value bodies do not. CanonicalInsert continues to own the String and never borrows projector storage.
design.failure: A get_ref/UTF8 conversion error resets all already-held/partially-updated values then returns the original error. Serialization error also resets values before propagation. Streaming aborts exactly as before; no catch/retry/new result is added. A deliberately reused projector can process a later valid row without stale contents, as the negative control specifies.
design.resource_limits: Existing check_row_size before conversion, serialized-row limit, checked cumulative canonical bytes, row count, ordinal, scratch page limits, current capacity-profile gates, CanonicalInsert64/8/1 and64KiB pending limit all remain unchanged. No changed512MiB output/plan or external supervisor budget.
design.legacy_api: project_row signature and returned owned Value remain unchanged; canonical and reference_spool callers remain source-compatible.

control_design.name: reused_projection_keeps_exact_sql_value_bytes_and_only_its_layout
control_design.independent_expectation: Literal JSON parsed into Value and serialized only to respect the same compiled Map-order feature. No SQL-value conversion helper derives expected values. Known empty-BLOB BLAKE3 digest af1349... is a literal.
covered: i64::MIN and i64::MAX preserving exact integers
UTF8 text with accented/non-Latin characters, embedded NUL, newline and quotation
continuous changes of SQL type and nullness
same key String buffer addresses reused
owned row values cleared after successful serialization
separate one-column layout has no old keys
control_design.not_claimed: This control is prepared, not executed. Existing test suite covers additional tier/byte limits and row multiplicity; it has not been rerun.

control_design.name: projection_error_clears_partial_and_prior_values_before_recovery
covered: first valid row deliberately leaves old values populated
next row writes its first field then fails on invalid UTF8 in second field
original error spelling contains oracle UTF8
error equality between retained public wrapper and reused owner
all partial/old values reset to Null after error
subsequent valid NULL/integer row yields exact literal JSON with no old value
control_design.production_boundary: Spool still returns the first error; this test probes helper state integrity and does not add runtime recovery/retry.

independence_limit: The original reference_spool body is byte-for-byte preserved, but its project_row callee now delegates to the shared new owner. Actual==reference alone would therefore be same-owner evidence. The added literal expected values and UTF8 failure/dirty-state controls are the separate semantic anchors; no second production converter was introduced.
existing_controls_preserved: All original streaming test function bodies, limits, check_row_size, CanonicalInsert, sorted traversal, equal_rows/Value fallback, duplicate ordinals, digests/examples and canonical implementation after project_row are exact original bytes.

performance_evidence_boundary.claim: The prior aggregate makes oracle allocation an appropriate engineering target, but does not measure how much parity time is spent on Map allocation. No speedup or100k/pass claim.

integration_boundary: Unreferenced blobs only. Non-author review and actual original controls must precede any independent source-admission chain. The candidate is not added to frozen176G, and no old A23/G2/D0 measurement is relabeled.

review_feedback_change.reason: Use ordinary method-call deref instead of relying on String::as_ptr associated-item resolution. This is a reviewer-identified compile risk avoided before execution, not a claimed reproduced compiler error.

metadata_correction.reason: Replace an estimated minute with the actual clock observation; source blobs unchanged.
